original_question: Can the bigraded algebraic transfer tau^{*,*} be realized as the edge homomorphism of a spectral sequence in a way that gives a sensible measure of how far tau^{*,*} is from being an isomorphism of bigraded algebras?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 3.2: Nick Kuhn's question asking whether the Singer transfer τ^{*,*} can be viewed as the edge homomorphism of some spectral sequence. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020p.pdf?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact mathematical target almost verbatim: it asks about realizing τ^{*,*} as an edge homomorphism of a spectral sequence and about using that realization to measure the failure of τ^{*,*} to be an isomorphism of bigraded algebras. Those are precisely the two ideas stated in Problem 3.2.
missing_details: Identify τ^{*,*} explicitly as the Singer transfer.
State the ambient prime p and that A is the mod-p Steenrod algebra.
Give the bidegree-wise definition of the transfer: τ_{s,t}: Hom_A^{t-s}(H^*((Z/p)^s; F_p), F_p)^{GL_s(Z/p)} -> Ext_A^{s,t}(F_p, F_p).
Clarify that τ^{*,*} denotes the family (or total bigraded map) formed from the τ_{s,t} over all bidegrees (s,t).
Make explicit that the source involves GL_s(Z/p)-invariants and degree-(t-s) A-linear homomorphisms.
Preserve the paper's intentional non-specificity: it asks for 'some spectral sequence' and does not specify filtration, convergence target, or which page produces the edge map.
State the purpose exactly as in the paper: to obtain a sensible measure of the failure of τ^{*,*} to be an isomorphism of bigraded algebras.
refined_question: Let p be a prime, let A be the mod-p Steenrod algebra, and let τ_{s,t}: Hom_A^{t-s}(H^*((Z/p)^s; F_p), F_p)^{GL_s(Z/p)} -> Ext_A^{s,t}(F_p, F_p) denote the Singer transfer. Can the resulting bigraded transfer τ^{*,*} be realized as the edge homomorphism of some spectral sequence, in a way that provides a sensible measure of the extent to which τ^{*,*} fails to be an isomorphism of bigraded algebras?
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of Problem 3.2 on page 438. The same section immediately precedes it with the displayed definition of the Singer transfer τ_{s,t}, which supplies the notation, source, target, and ambient prime/Steenrod algebra that the draft leaves implicit. The paper also explicitly says that the problem is 'not so well posed', so a faithful refinement should keep the spectral sequence unspecified rather than adding convergence, filtration, or page-level requirements that the paper itself does not impose. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020p.pdf?utm_source=openai))
